html:
Talietumu is a stone fort on the island of Wallis (ʻUvea), built around the 15th century by warriors from Tonga who conquered the island. Its walls and platforms are among the largest ancient remains on the island.

In this period the rulers of the Tuʻi Tonga reached out across western Polynesia, and Wallis came under Tongan chiefs. The Wallisian language and the island's chiefly titles still carry Tongan marks.

Wallis later kept its own kings, the Lavelua, who still hold office today under France after the islands became a French territory.
